answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, recurring stake rather than the number of agent identities: each agent locks a deposit and earns voting weight only as it completes independently verified work over time. If an agent cheats, the kernel of the system can slash its deposit and revoke its accrued weight. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many deposits and keep each identity active through the tide of verification rounds, tying up capital and labor; identities cannot simply wander in and out for free.
